nodes.summary: A group $G$ has test rank $r \in \mathbb{N}$ when $G$ has a test set of cardinality $r$ and every test set of $G$ has cardinality at least $r$ (an infinite set counting as having cardinality $\infty$), that is, when the minimum of the cardinalities of the test sets of $G$ is $r$.
nodes.title: Test rank of a group

nodes.summary: A subset $S$ of a group $G$ is a test set when every endomorphism of $G$ that fixes every element of $S$ is bijective, that is, an automorphism of $G$.
nodes.title: Test set of a group

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. The free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ is the quotient $F_r / V_W(F_r)$ of the free group $F_r$ on $r$ generators by its verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ for $W$.
nodes.title: Relatively free group as a quotient of a free group

nodes.summary: Let $F_\mathbb{N}$ be the free group on countably many generators and $W \subseteq F_\mathbb{N}$ a set of words, the laws. A group $G$ satisfies the laws $W$ when $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every $w \in W$ and every homomorphism $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to G$, that is, every law takes the value $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. The variety defined by $W$ is the class of these groups.
nodes.title: Groups satisfying a set of laws in countably many variables

nodes.summary: Resolved false: the same variety (`[[x, y], z] = 1`, `[x, y]^p = 1`, `p` prime) is not periodic since it contains `ℤ`, its free groups of every rank `r ≥ 1` have test rank `r` (Kinyon-Urban, Proposition 3.9), and it is not the variety of all abelian groups since it contains the non-abelian group `UT₃(𝔽_p)`. nodes.title: Timoshenko's test rank question, part (b)

nodes.summary: There is a set $W$ of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators such that for every $r \ge 1$ the free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ has test rank $r$, but the variety is not abelian: some group satisfying the laws $W$ is not abelian.
nodes.title: Negative answer to Timoshenko's test rank question, part (a)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every set $W$ of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, if for every $r \ge 1$ the free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ has test rank $r$, then this variety is abelian: every group satisfying the laws $W$ is abelian.
nodes.title: Timoshenko's test rank question, part (a)

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $F_r$ be the free group on $r$ generators. The verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ of $F_r$ for $W$ is the normal closure in $F_r$ of all elements $\varphi(w)$ with $w \in W$ and $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to F_r$ a homomorphism.
